problem_restatement: Reconstruct whether the 38 closes attributed to hype_breakout_onset_bidirectional_v1 are one comparable HYPE experiment or a mixture of native HYPE and later cross-asset authorities.
lineage_findings: The first seven entries executed only on HYPE under one exact HYPE asset-wrapper fingerprint, but spanned three cohort fingerprints and five process runs.
Rows eight and nine retained HYPE-only execution but changed maximum notional from $25 to $75.
V14 and V25 granted the legacy provider execution authority on BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE without asset-native qualification.
V39 retired HYPE from the legacy provider while continuing BTC, ETH, and SOL under the same strategy ID.
The first three native lifecycles do not persist an execution plan; exact 8h-soft/24h-hard extension authority is therefore not proven for those rows.
All seven first entries were autonomous; the later mixed sample includes manual and cross-provider exits.
The 38-trade aggregate is valid accounting history but invalid as a controlled strategy continuation.

decision.reason: The first seven support the user's scope-drift diagnosis, but seven trades do not establish durable edge; the closest later HYPE-only continuation was 0W/2L after sizing changed, and the preregistered native reconstruction was later rejected prospectively.
decision.next_investigation: Keep current V57 HYPE evidence collection intact and test only a materially distinct preregistered HYPE mechanism; do not reuse the 38-trade aggregate as promotion evidence.

reopen_conditions: An immutable pre-entry source bundle proves exact provider and execution-plan parity across the first seven and a later HYPE-only sample.
A preregistered independent HYPE-only sample is positive after exact costs and after removing its largest winner.
A materially distinct causal HYPE mechanism survives development, untouched validation, holdout, and source-compatible prospective translation.
risks_and_failure_modes: The first seven may be a favorable small-sample streak.
Profile, sizing, market regime, and exit authority changed together, so their individual causal effects are not identifiable from live history alone.
Current provider-source parity supports later entry semantics but cannot prove the exact first-seven provider bytes.
Dollar PnL is not directly comparable across the $25 and $75 sizing regimes.
falsifier: Update this report if immutable raw fills change the 38-lifecycle population, a pre-entry bundle proves a different exact first-seven provider contract, or a matched HYPE-only autonomous later cohort was omitted.
